what: The XML Formatter makes XML readable with consistent indentation, shrinks it to a single line, or checks that it is well-formed, showing the exact line and column of the first error.

It works with any XML: configuration files, SVG, RSS and Atom feeds, sitemaps, SOAP messages, Android layouts, Office XML parts and more. Comments, CDATA, processing instructions and the DOCTYPE are preserved.
uses: Pretty-print a compact XML response to understand its structure.
Find the missing or mismatched tag that stops a config file or feed from loading.
Minify XML before sending or embedding it.
Format an SVG to edit it by hand, with long tags split over lines.
Make sure an RSS feed or sitemap is well-formed before publishing.
tutorial: Paste it, or press Open file to load an .xml, .svg, .rss, .kml, .gpx or similar file.
Pick 2 spaces, 4 spaces or a tab.
Remove comments, write empty elements as <tag/>, or put each attribute on its own line for long tags.
Press Format for readable XML or Minify for a single line.
If the XML is not well-formed, the message gives the line and column and the box below shows the lines around it with a marker.
features: Uses your browser's XML parser and shows the line, column and surrounding code.
Text mixed with tags, CDATA, comments, the declaration and DOCTYPE stay exactly as written.
The result is parsed again before it replaces your text.
Optionally puts attributes of long tags on separate lines.
Several megabytes in a few seconds, without uploading anything.

example.text: Paste text and press Format. The message says Invalid XML at line 1 with the mismatched closing tag, and the marker points at . Change it to and press Format again to get a neatly indented file.

tips: Validate only checks without changing your text.

HTML is not XML: entities like   and unclosed tags such as
are errors in XML.
Use Minify before embedding XML in code or URLs.
Keep a copy of the original if you remove comments.
problems: XML knows only & < > " and '. Write other characters directly or as numbers like  .
An XML document must have exactly one top-level element. Wrap everything in one root tag.
Only text files up to 30 MB can be opened. Binary files such as .docx must be unzipped first.
